title: Skill-anchored scope bundles and probabilistic triage for cycle staffing
creator: Ethan Rivera
description:
Summary: Introduce a lightweight, repeatable approach to slice cycle-level initiatives into 'skill-anchored scope bundles' (SASBs) and apply a probabilistic overcommit model to drive objective scope cuts and contingency reserves. Goal is to reduce mid-cycle scope churn, improve predictability of OKR delivery, and make staffing trade-offs explicit for PMs and Eng leads.

Why now: We are seeing repeated mid-cycle de-scoping where skills are over-subscribed and optimistic point assumptions lead to >30% chance of missing committed outcomes. Current playbooks are manual and inconsistent across initiatives.

What SASBs are: each SASB is an independently valuable outcome bundle sized to a single planning unit (2-8 points) and annotated with: primary skill vector (e.g., infra:2, frontend:1, ml-ops:1), risk_score (0-100), external_dependency_flag, and OKR-mapped outcome. Bundles are prioritized by value density (OKR-importance / risk-adjusted points).

Probabilistic triage model: we will estimate per-skill supply for the cycle (FTE-equivalents), map bundle demand into skill-hours, and compute an overcommit probability using a simple Monte Carlo sampling of uncertainty around estimates (sigma = 20% default). The model returns: P(overcommit) and a ranked list of bundles whose removal reduces P(overcommit) most per lost OKR value.

Decision rules (proposed):
- If P(overcommit) <= 20%: commit full tranche and allocate 1.0 FTE-equivalent contingency per 10 planned points.
- If 20% < P(overcommit) <= 35%: apply targeted trim to low-value SASBs until P(overcommit) <= 20% or until 12% of planned points are deferred, whichever comes first.
- If P(overcommit) > 35%: escalate to product leadership for scope-revision and guarantee a 20% contingency reserve.

Operational changes:
- New cycle intake form for PMs to submit SASBs (Confluence template + Google Sheet).
- A lightweight python notebook and Google Sheet to run the Monte Carlo model (linked below).
- Add a 'Cycle Staffing' dashboard to Console with per-skill burn rates and overcommit probability widget.

Trade-offs considered:
- Simplicity vs precision: we prefer a conservative, easy-to-run model that teams will adopt over a complex deterministic optimizer.
- Contingency sizing is intentionally coarse to avoid gaming.
- Requires discipline up-front in defining skills and outcomes which adds ~1-2 hours per initiative intake.

Stakeholders: PM leads (Priya, Mateo), Eng leads (Ava Martinez, Jonah Lee), GtM for OKR alignment (Lena Ortiz), Data for modeling help (Marcus Chen).
acceptance_criteria: 1) SASB intake template published and used by >80% of initiatives in cycle intake. 2) Monte Carlo workbook available and validated by Data team; basic test case reproduces recent cycle overcommit scenario. 3) Dashboard prototype deployed to Console staging showing per-skill supply/demand and P(overcommit). 4) Two pilot initiatives use SASB process and show improved mid-cycle delta (target: reduce scope change events by 40% relative to last cycle).
updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting with PM/Eng leads. Agreed on single canonical skills list (frontend, backend, infra, ml, ml-ops, infra-sdlc, qa, ux). Action: Priya to publish SASB template by 2026-02-24.

2026-02-24: SASB Confluence template published (https://confluence.redwood/internal/cycle-sasb-template). Shared with initiative owners. Feedback: need explicit field for 'value density' and 'integration-risk'.

2026-03-01: Data sync. Marcus provided baseline skill supply estimates derived from last 3 cycles. Agreed default estimate uncertainty = 20% (sigma). Notebook skeleton posted: https://github.com/redwood-inc/cycle-models/pull/18.

2026-03-04: Prototype Monte Carlo sheet (read-only): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1abcDEF_sasb-demo. Early run on 'Search Latency' initiative showed P(overcommit)=38% with current staffing; model recommended deferring two low-value frontend bundles (combined 10 points) to bring P<=20%.

2026-03-07: PM review with product leadership. Decision: adopt decision-rule thresholds as proposed (20%/35%). Leadership requested pilot on two initiatives and a clear communications template for customers if de-scope affects SLA commitments.

2026-03-10: Engineering feedback: suggested adding 'skill-pairs' for cross-functional work (e.g., frontend+ml-ops) to capture handoff costs. Updated intake template v1.1 includes 'skill-pair' field. Notebook PR updated to accept pairs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inc/cycle-models/pull/21.

2026-03-12: Pilot kickoff: 'Vector Embeddings UX' and 'Dedicated Autoscaling' chosen for pilots. Priya assigned to run weekly model refresh and report in the Cycle triage channel. Next checkpoint 2026-03-18 to review pilot outputs and adjust thresholds if needed.
